```{r}
#Part 2 
#The Message - The graphs show the geometric means of U/Umsy and B/Bmsy where U = mortality, B = biommass and msy = maximum sustainable yield. The graph is a function of Management Intensity to those two variables. It is showing with increasing management intensity there is a lower U/Umsy and a higher B/Bmsy. Essentially showing that lowering mortality of the stocks can increase biomass of the stocks. 

#Flaws - The 0 on the graphs are not lined up to the bottom of the graph. The Y-axis is also connected between the two graphs when they are representing two different variables and values. I do not think the two graphs being attached help with any interpretations of the graph. The points are means yet the graphs have no standard error lines. 
```


```{r}
library(ggplot2)
#https://www.pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.1909726116#data-availability
data <- read.csv("../data/workshop3/Workshop3Data.csv")
attach(data)
plot1 <- ggplot(data = data, aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_point() +
  xlab("Management Intensity") +
  ylab("U/Umsy") +
  theme_classic() +
 scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 3)) 
plot1
```
